newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Sterling bond to be placed Wednesday - source.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Sterling bond to be placed Wednesday - source.

text.p: The United Mexican States (UMS) will place a 300 million five-year sterling bond on Wednesday, a government source said on Tuesday.
It will be the first sterling bond for the Mexican federal government since 1991, but fits with the government's strategy of placing debt issues in various currencies.
"It was the market that presented the best yield," the source, who declined to be identified, said.
The bond will be priced at a tight range, perhaps about 170 to 180 basis points over gilts, market sources said.
Lead managers will be BZW and SBC Warburg.
Other Mexican borrowers tied to the government have gone to the sterling market since the 1991 UMS issue, however.
Mexican development bank Bancomext issued a seven-year sterling bond in 1993. Mexican state-owned oil giant Petroleos Mexicanos issued a 10-year Sterling bond in 1993 as well.

So far this year, Mexico has placed a wide variety of debt issues, including a 10-year $1.0 billion global bond, a 12-year 1.5 billion mark bond, two yen issues, and two Italian lira issues, one with a 10-year term and the other a 20-year issue.
Since returning to debt markets after the peso crash in 1994, the UMS has steadily built yield curves in Italian lira, Japanese yen, Deutschemarks, as well as U.S. dollars.
